items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: I don't know these boys only by reputation

ctx.x: Well, not as much as Eddie, because Eddie was fortunate enough to make this European tour, which really had much to do with his success, because he was a huge success at that time. But I have had quite a bit of success with most of the pupils I had at that time. But they didn't go in for concert work. They did most orchestra work. It was Jimmy Bell. And when they had the orchestra at the Regal Theatre, we had a couple of boys in there. I can't think of their names now. To get back to some of the other…
...and the other instruments, like on trumpet...

You of course heard a lot of King Oliver and Freddie Keppard, and of course Louis Armstrong, all of those New Orleans trumpet players, so many great ones that I don't know which one you can pick. Oh yes, there are a lot of

items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Somebody told me that Joe Oliver's the widow, Stella Oliver has one in New Orleans. I haven't had her. Is that so? So we'll get to see her, maybe she'll have one. [INTERVIEWEE] Uh-huh.

ctx.x: We had Joe, the same boy. See, I didn't change very much. You didn't change? No, no, no. Those boys stayed with me right on through. The clarinet, do you remember? I was playing Clown Insect for myself. Oh, you were playing Clown Insect for yourself. Yeah. And after the second week, he said, well, I'm afraid we're going to have to dismiss you because she's complaining too much. I said, well, that was the agreement, it's all right. Well, we were there just long enough to have won over the young dancers, all of the…
